channel.title: Educational AI Daily
channel.description: Artificial intelligence, as told by three teaching communities

item.title: The Council of the EU approves conclusions on citizens’ AI skills
item.description: Member states back the idea that people of all ages should learn to use artificial intelligence critically and responsibly. These are policy guidelines, not a rule that binds schools.

media:content.media:description: A diagram of three steps joined by arrows: a building with columns, “European framework”; a flag, “Each state”; and an open book, “Classrooms”. The dotted red arrow between the last two is labelled “Guidance only”.

item.title: Chicago weighs its options if Google withdraws search from districts that reject its AI
item.description: According to the Chicago Sun-Times, Google warns that school districts that do not allow its AI tools will lose access to search next year.

media:content.media:description: A building, “District”, with an arrow labelled “Rejects AI” pointing to a magnifying glass crossed out with a red circle, “Search”, and below it the question “No access?”.

item.title: A Catalan-language train puzzle for planning shunting moves is new in the repository
item.description: The Vibe Coding Educativo resource repository adds eight resources in the week ending 20 November: one is presented here and seven have already had their own article.

media:content.media:description: Welcome screen of the game over a track layout with colourful numbered wagons, with a field for typing a player name.

item.title: Manchester Animation Festival will not accept films made with generative AI from 2027
item.description: The British festival announced it on 13 November together with this year’s awards. Its director presents it as a way of backing animation artists.

media:content.media:description: A film clapperboard, “AI film”, with an arrow labelled “From 2027” cut by a red bar that does not reach the building with columns, “Festival”.

item.title: Trama adds readings grouped into “universes” and versions of different difficulty
item.description: The reading-comprehension catalogue lets you choose readings that share the same world and versions of the same text at different levels. Its author asks for help translating it into Galician, Basque and Aranese.

media:content.media:description: On the left, three open books inside a dotted circle, “Universe”; on the right, three stacked sheets with lines of text of different lengths, “Variants”.

item.title: From 9% to 36% in research-level physics: AI still fails almost two in three
item.description: In November 2025 a new evaluation of unseen physics problems was launched, and no AI model reached 10%. A year later, the best result is close to 36%.

media:content.media:description: Diptych in two halves. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, a sheet with three physics challenges, all three crossed out, and the label “Fails almost everything”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same sheet with the first challenge solved, with a blue mark, and the other two still crossed out, with the label “Still fails a lot”.

item.title: Gemini will separate conversation history from permission to train models
item.description: Google will replace the “Keep Activity” setting with two: one for history and, separately, one that lets its models use the content of conversations.

media:content.media:description: A switch labelled “Keep Activity” splits, with two arrows, into two independent settings: “History”, with a calendar and a switch, and “Training”, with a cogwheel and another switch.

item.title: Google AI Studio builds complete Android apps from a description
item.description: It generates Kotlin apps with sign-in and a database, tests them in an in-browser emulator and lets you install them from your personal Google Play library.

media:content.media:description: A speech bubble labelled “Description” leads, with an arrow, to a browser window with a phone inside, labelled “Emulator”, and from there, with another arrow, to a box with a play symbol, labelled “Google Play”.

item.title: Genie 4 comes to Project Genie: interactive worlds that change as you explore them
item.description: Access starts with Google AI Ultra, and AI Pro subscribers can join a waiting list.

media:content.media:description: Two framed landscapes, labelled “World” and “Modified”: the first, with mountains and a sun; the second, the same mountains with a cloud and rain. Between them, an arrow labelled “New command” with a speech bubble below.

item.title: Canada launches a national AI literacy initiative with three strands: students, teachers and the public
item.description: The Canadian government has launched, with the Amii institute, a national AI literacy initiative with three training strands, one of them yet to launch. The document shared in the library presents it and points out its shortcomings.

media:content.media:description: Diagram: a box on the left, “AI literacy”, from which three paths lead, each with an icon: a graduation cap labelled “Students”, a whiteboard labelled “Teachers” and a group of people labelled “Citizens”; beneath the last one, a dashed line labelled “Yet to launch”.

item.title: The 1994 Clark–Kozma debate helps in reading Stanford’s studies on AI
item.description: An academic argument over whether technology influences learning or only the method matters, recalled in the group in connection with Stanford’s review.

media:content.media:description: A drawing divided into two halves. On the left, a package labelled “Method” on a lorry labelled “Medium”, with the name “Clark”: the medium only carries the method. On the right, two overlapping circles, with the name “Kozma”: medium and method cannot be separated.

item.title: A teacher reflective journal with AI raises the question of whether the assistant supports or replaces judgement
item.description: A master’s thesis project proposes dictating after each class and having an assistant organise the text and return questions; the group debates whether that weakens judgement.

media:content.media:description: A microphone labelled “Dictation” leads to a document labelled “Summary” and to a speech bubble with a question mark labelled “Questions”. An arrow goes down from the document to a box labelled “The teacher decides”.

item.title: Free ChatGPT for teachers only in the US: a year on, the border remains
item.description: In November 2025, OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teachers and Spanish teachers wondered whether it would reach them. A year on, it has grown in US schools, but it has not crossed the ocean.

media:content.media:description: Diptych. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a globe with a single pin on “US” and a closed padlock below. On the right, “Today”: the same globe with three blue pins on “US” and the padlock still closed, next to the label “Spain”.

item.title: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper introduced on 12 November, now has “Laboratorio XR: Ensayo…
item.description: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper introduced on 12 November, now has “Laboratorio XR: Ensayo a la llama” (an XR flame-test lab) and a simulation of the human eye online. The page does not explain the lab’s requirements or say who makes it.

item.title: Stanford gathers 52 causal studies on AI in schools and sees uneven results
item.description: The November review goes from 20 to 52 studies and concludes that AI looks more promising for understanding new material than for producing assignments, but no use improves learning consistently.

media:content.media:description: Diagram: a person uses an assistant, from which two paths lead: one towards “Understand” and another, in red, towards “Do the task”, and at the end a balance. Labels: Assistant, Understand, Do the task, Uneven.

item.title: Galicia’s parliament passes the law regulating phones, screens and AI in classrooms
item.description: The Digital Education Law limits individual use of devices up to the fifth year of primary school and was passed with the votes of the PPdeG and the opposition of the BNG and the PSdeG.

media:content.media:description: Diagram: a parliament building leads to a law, from which come a phone crossed out in red and a video camera. Labels: Parliament, Digital law, Phones, No recording.

item.title: Madrid adds to EducaMadrid an AI agent that prepares personalised materials
item.description: According to the Community of Madrid, the agent was developed by civil servants in its regional digital ministry and can be used by teachers in publicly funded schools.

media:content.media:description: Diagram: a teacher uses an agent, from which three results come: a document, a tick and an envelope. Labels: Teacher, Agent, Notes, Quizzes, Emails.

item.title: Experiment with 400 adults finds a Socratic AI tutor teaches more than explaining the mistake
item.description: Carnegie Mellon researchers compare four ways of giving feedback after a mistake and suggest that what works is sending the student back to the task until they get it right.

media:content.media:description: Two paths after a mistake, marked with a red cross. At the top, the mistake leads to a box labelled “Explanation” and from there to the next problems. At the bottom, the mistake leads to “Question”, then to “Retry”, with an arrow returning from “Retry” to “Question” until the answer is right, and finally to a tick under the label “Success”. Above, the label “64%”.

item.title: Suno launches Visuals to create lyric videos and cover art from its songs
item.description: The feature generates clips of up to 15 seconds and is paid for with credits separate from those for songs.

media:content.media:description: Diagram: a musical note with three arrows towards three cards: a video clapperboard, an image and a camera. Labels: Song, Lyric video, Cover art, 15 s clip, Credits sold separately.

item.title: A teacher measures the use of their apps with Umami, cookie-free statistics
item.description: This tool shows which features students use without collecting names or email addresses.

media:content.media:description: Diagram: an app window with a pointer clicking sends its usage to a dashboard with a crossed-out eye; beside it, a cookie crossed out in red and a flag. Labels: App, Umami, No cookies, Error flag.

item.title: Antigravity buckled under demand at its free launch; a year on, it has paid plans
item.description: In November 2025, Google’s agent-based coding environment launched, free and overwhelmed. A year later it is on version 2.32, and extra usage requires a subscription.

media:content.media:description: Diptych with two identical windows. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a window with a warning triangle and the label “Overloaded”. On the right, “Today”: the same window with a blue padlock and the labels “Weekly limits” and “Pro and Ultra”.

item.title: Google is rolling out temporary threads in AI Mode in its search engine: the questions in those…
item.description: Google is rolling out temporary threads in AI Mode in its search engine: the questions in those conversations are not saved in the history or used for personalisation, according to its announcement of 17 November.

item.title: Trama now has 245 reading texts in Catalan and Spanish, from the third year of primary school to the first…
item.description: Trama now has 245 reading texts in Catalan and Spanish, from the third year of primary school to the first year of ESO, according to its own website.

item.title: ChatGPT Learn publishes a guide to giving tasks to GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in Codex, OpenAI’s programming…
item.description: ChatGPT Learn publishes a guide to giving tasks to GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in Codex, OpenAI’s programming assistant; the page does not state a launch date or plans.

item.title: Kling AI announces Kling Image 4.0, with images generated directly in 8K resolution, text in several…
item.description: Kling AI announces Kling Image 4.0, with images generated directly in 8K resolution, text in several languages and up to 10 mutually consistent images per request, according to its statement of 17 November; it does not state availability or prices.

item.title: Gemini Notebook turns a notebook’s sources into an interactive website
item.description: All it takes is typing “make me a site” in the notebook’s chat. Members of the groups have already tried it, and one has uploaded the result to Moodle.

media:content.media:description: Diagram from left to right: three documents labelled “Sources” go into a notebook with a chat bubble labelled “make me a site”; out of it comes a web page with a panel and lines of text, labelled “Website”, which is downloaded as a “.html” file and uploaded to “Moodle”.

item.title: Three apps in Catalan: a classroom auction and two density labs
item.description: Felip Sarroca i Gil shares Subhasta, for working on scarcity and budgeting, and Densitats and Densitat, for studying flotation with Archimedes’ principle.

media:content.media:description: On the left, an auctioneer’s gavel on its block, with coins, labelled “Auction”. On the right, a tank of water in which a block floats, with an upward arrow labelled “Buoyancy” and the label “Flotation”.

item.title: Agente Clima IES analyses classroom temperature and humidity in the browser
item.description: The app reads sensor logs and compares them with the limits set by the regulation on workplaces.

media:content.media:description: A document labelled “CSV” passes into a browser window, labelled “In the browser”, containing a thermometer with the label “17–27 °C” and water drops with the label “30–70%”.

item.title: Google Flow will retire Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Quality and Omni Flash 1.1 on 5 December
item.description: Flow’s help page recommends moving to Omni Flash 1.2 or Veo 3.1 Lite for future projects.

media:content.media:description: A calendar crossed out in red, labelled “5 Dec”, heads two groups of clapperboards: on the left, three labelled “Being retired”; on the right, two labelled “Omni Flash 1.2” and “Veo 3.1 Lite”, under the label “Staying”.

item.title: Grading a text prepared with AI requires a sample of the student’s own writing
item.description: Asking students to explain how they used artificial intelligence makes sense if they know the rules before they start. Giving a mark takes something more, even when the declaration is entirely sincere.

item.title: Scholar Labs goes from a waiting list and English only to opening up in every language
item.description: In November 2025, Scholar Labs accepted questions only in English and many people had to join a waiting list. Since June 2026 it has been open to every signed-in user and accepts questions in all languages.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a closed padlock with the labels “Waiting list” and “English only”. On the right, “Today”: an open padlock, in blue, with the label “All languages” and the translation icon.

item.title: South Korea will check all glasses at the university entrance exam (Suneung) after the top scorer in the…
item.description: South Korea will check all glasses at the university entrance exam (Suneung) after the top scorer in the tax accountant exam confessed to using a micro-camera and generative AI to cheat. According to The Next Web, more than 500,000 students sit the exam at 1,300 centres.

item.title: A robotic palletising cell is simulated in the browser and exports the scene as .glb
item.description: According to the message of the person who shared it, the app was built with AI models; it lets users stop, resume and monitor a virtual industrial cell and export the scene for Blender.

media:content.media:description: Diagram from left to right: a browser window with a robotic cell (conveyor with boxes, robot arm and pallet) and a vertical red line marking the safety curtain; a blue arrow towards a 3D cube. Labels: “Cell in the browser”, “Light curtain”, “.glb” and “Blender”.

item.title: INTEF updates its guide to AI in education with ten ethical principles and a phased plan for schools to adopt it
item.description: Version 2.0 of the Ministry of Education's guide, published in September 2026, organises the use of AI around three profiles (students, teachers and schools) and adds annexes ready for the classroom.

media:content.media:description: Three cards, each with a human figure, labelled “Students”, “Teachers” and “School”, resting on a base labelled “Three profiles”; above the school card a seven-step staircase labelled “Seven phases” rises to a circle with a review arrow.

item.title: Trama offers 206 reading texts with questions for building reading comprehension worksheets
item.description: The catalogue, in Catalan and Spanish, is aimed mainly at the fourth to sixth years of primary school and lets teachers choose the questions before printing the worksheet or downloading it as a PDF.

media:content.media:description: Trama's catalogue of reading texts with filters on the left and cards showing an illustration, title, school year, difficulty and a “Prepara la fitxa” button.

item.title: EyeJack Creator: bringing an image to life on your phone with augmented reality
item.description: A website lets you attach a video or animation to an image and watch it on your phone by pointing at it. The free version limits views, duration and size.

media:content.media:description: Diagram in two halves. On the left, “Before”: a poster with a drawn sun and mountain, a QR code and a phone pointing at it, labelled “Poster”. On the right, “After”: the same poster with motion lines and a phone showing the animated drawing, labelled “In motion”.

item.title: Failed for studying from flawed ChatGPT notes; today Catalonia has 45 guidelines on use
item.description: In November 2025, a Catalan teacher said he had failed students who studied from flawed notes made with ChatGPT, and the group called for literacy and rules. A year later, the Departament d’Educació has set out how AI should enter schools.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a document crossed out with an X, labelled “Flawed notes”. On the right, “Today”: the same document marked with a blue check mark, labelled “45 guidelines”.

item.title: ElevenLabs’ video translator page advertises more than 90 languages, although its FAQ section speaks of…
item.description: ElevenLabs’ video translator page advertises more than 90 languages, although its FAQ section speaks of more than 29 and does not mention Catalan. It states a limit of one minute or 50 MB per file.

item.title: Declaring AI use: a teacher asks schools to clarify which uses are acceptable
item.description: A teacher asks whether schools, very focused on detecting AI-generated work, explain clearly enough which uses are acceptable and how to declare them.

media:content.media:description: Diagram with the question “Which uses are allowed?” at the top. On the left, a document with a blue arrow leading to a scale, under the label “Declared process”. On the right, a document with an arrow leading to a red question mark, under the label “Hidden process”.

item.title: Chrome publishes Modern Web Guidance 1.0, a guide to the current web for coding agents
item.description: The guide brings together expert-verified solutions and compatibility data to correct the outdated knowledge of models.

media:content.media:description: Three boxes joined by arrows: a file with a clock, labelled “Old data”, an open book guide, labelled “Current web guide”, and a code file with a red tick, labelled “Current code”.

item.title: Battleships in Catalan, against the machine or online with a room code
item.description: “Enfonsar la flota” is a web version of the classic battleships game, with a 10×10 board, which works on coordinates and strategy in primary and secondary school.

media:content.media:description: Start screen of the game with two cards: “Partida en línia”, with a button to create a room and a code field, and “Contra la màquina”, with three difficulty levels.

item.title: Antigravity adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen and an Orchestrator mode that shares out the work
item.description: Orchestrator combines Hydrogen with more powerful models; access depends on Google’s paid plan.

media:content.media:description: Under the title “Orchestrator”, two boxes: on the left one with a branching diagram, labelled “Carbon plans”, and on the right one with a code file, labelled “Hydrogen edits”. An arrow carries the work from the first to the second and a red arrow goes back, labelled “If it gets stuck”.

item.title: Seedream 5.5 promises to keep an image stable across 100 rounds of editing
item.description: ByteDance presents a version of its image generator designed for retouching the same image again and again without changing what is left untouched, and which generates transparent backgrounds.

media:content.media:description: Under the title “Seedream 5.5”, an image passes through circular arrows, labelled “100 rounds”, and comes out the same as it went in. On the right, a blue circle on a background of alternating squares, labelled “Transparent background”.

item.title: Cross-checking several AIs was a homemade trick; today Perplexity does it in a single query
item.description: In November 2025, the advice for trusting an answer was to ask two or three artificial intelligences and use another to look for the discrepancies. In February 2026, Perplexity turned that method into a feature.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: three answers from three AIs that a person, drawn with head and shoulders and labelled “By hand”, compares. On the right, “Today”: the same three answers go into a single blue box with two zones, “Agree”, with a tick, and “Differ”.

item.title: According to the Financial Times, reported by Deseret News, Spotify is preparing for early 2027 a paid…
item.description: According to the Financial Times, reported by Deseret News, Spotify is preparing for early 2027 a paid add-on ($4 to $5 a month, according to that report) to create AI remixes and covers, with agreements with Universal, Merlin and Believe. Spotify has confirmed neither date nor price; in August it had already announced the project with Universal and Merlin.

item.title: Intelética, IBERAMIA’s open-access journal on artificial intelligence, ethics and society, accepts…
item.description: Intelética, IBERAMIA’s open-access journal on artificial intelligence, ethics and society, accepts articles in Spanish, Portuguese and English.

item.title: AI-text detectors are not proof, and institutions propose assessing the process instead
item.description: Programs that promise to reveal whether a piece of work was written by artificial intelligence get it wrong, including for students who have not used it, and even their own makers advise against punishing anyone on their say-so. This report explains what the studies, the European Regulation, data protection authorities and education guidelines say, and sets out a no-cost plan for assessing fairly in any subject: state which uses are allowed, ask for evidence of the process and listen to students.

media:content.media:description: Two-column infographic. On the left, under the label “Detector”, a document with a percentage bar and a question mark, and three warnings (an alert triangle, two speech bubbles and a half-and-half box) representing false positives, poorer results in a second language and failures with mixed texts; below, the label “Indication, not proof”. An arrow leads to the right, under the label “Process”, where four steps in a staircase labelled “Declared uses”, “Drafts”, “In stages” and “Oral explanation” lead to a person holding a scale and the label “A person decides”.

item.title: A teacher asks Codex to model Industrial Revolution machines in Blender
item.description: Felip Sarroca i Gil says his computer cannot open Blender, but Codex can operate it, and it has generated 3D models for his website for fourth-year ESO students.

media:content.media:description: A diagram from left to right: a speech bubble labelled “Request” leads to a cog labelled “Codex + Blender”, which leads to a cube with three dots labelled “3D model”; a curved red arrow, labelled “More realism”, returns from the model to the request.

item.title: GeoBreath guides breathing exercises with geometric shapes and an adjustable rhythm
item.description: Luis Vilela Acuña's app uses an animated shape to show when to breathe in, hold and breathe out. It opens in the browser, with nothing to install, and is available in six languages.

media:content.media:description: GeoBreath screen with a square along whose sides a dot travels, the prompt “Inspira” in the centre, the session and cycle counters and the selector for shape and seconds per side.

item.title: A web editor lets teachers design collectable fauna and flora cards for the classroom
item.description: The Eco-Duel Card Generator, created by David Cordones, offers a form for composing cards with data on animals and plants, with one collection per school year, from the first year of primary to the second year of Bachillerato.

media:content.media:description: Card editor with the form on the left and, on the right, a fauna card called Senglar with size 7, level 3 and speed 5, and the buttons Descarregar and Copiar above it.

item.title: Gemini came and went in educational accounts; today the school switches it on or off
item.description: In November 2025, anyone using Gemini with an educational account could not tell which features they would find from one day to the next. A year later, Google has opened up features that were then denied to them, but for students’ accounts each school will decide.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: two rows, “Gmail” with a video and a tick, and “XTEC” with a video and a red cross. On the right, “Today”: two school buildings, one with a switch turned on and the other with one turned off, next to the label “School”.

item.title: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper presented on 12 November, has a 3D simulation for…
item.description: Eduvers, the simulation platform that the paper presented on 12 November, has a 3D simulation for preparing a NaOH solution and measuring the acidity of vinegar, according to its description.

item.title: Wharton releases Primer, an open system that turns a conversation into a simulation
item.description: Wharton Generative AI Labs offers an open-source prototype in which a team of agents interviews the teacher and builds a simulation for students. Its authors warn that it has not been evaluated in classrooms.

media:content.media:description: A diagram in two boxes: on the left, a teacher labelled “Teacher” hands over their conversation and receives a document with an approval mark, labelled “Design”; on the right, a student, labelled “Student”, talks to a character, labelled “Character”; below, a red arrow labelled “Report” returns from the simulation to the teacher.

item.title: INTEF to present the 2026 update of its AI guide at SIMO on 13 November
item.description: According to INTEF’s programme at SIMO EDUCACIÓN, that day was to see the presentation of the new version of its guide on the use of AI in education and another on how to integrate it into schools.

media:content.media:description: A timeline under the label “13 November” with two sessions: at “10:30”, an open book labelled “AI guide”, and at “13:30”, a document labelled “Schools”.

item.title: Conservatoire regulations, indicators and classroom games, new in the repository
item.description: The Vibe Coding Educativo resource repository adds 25 resources this week: 13 are presented here and 12 have already had their own article.

media:content.media:description: Home page of the Legis CPMDEM catalogue with a search box, filters for validity and categories of regulation, and the first entries for decrees and orders.

item.title: ElevenLabs’ Scribe v3 cuts Spanish errors by 35%, according to the company
item.description: ElevenLabs’ new speech-to-text models reduce word errors compared with Scribe v2. The figures are the company’s own.

media:content.media:description: On the left, a sound wave labelled “Voice” turns into a sheet with lines of text labelled “Text”; on the right, two columns labelled “Scribe v2” and “Scribe v3”, the second one shorter, with a red downward arrow and the label “−35%”.

item.title: Atlas en xogo, a map game in Galician, joins EDUmind’s apps
item.description: A new interactive geography app in Galician has been shared in Vibe Coding Educativo. A full description of its game modes could not be checked.

media:content.media:description: A browser window with a map and the label “Atlas en xogo”; to its left, a magnifying glass with a plus sign, labelled “Zoom”; to its right, a globe labelled “3D view”.

item.title: Disney was going to open its characters to AI; Sora shut down before the money arrived
item.description: In November 2025 it was being said that Disney would allow content to be created with its characters, and the end of generative AI’s “free-for-all” was being predicted. The deal came in December, with Sora; in March, OpenAI shut Sora down and the deal fell apart.

media:content.media:description: Diptych in two halves. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a film clapperboard and a coin with a dollar sign, under the label “Licence”. On the right, “Today”: the same clapperboard and the same coin crossed out with blue lines, under the label “Closed”.

item.title: Microsoft unveils Classroom, a dedicated space to centre classwork on Microsoft 365
item.description: Microsoft Classroom brings assignments, grades and AI tools together on a single screen for primary, secondary and higher education. It arrives in 2027 at no extra cost for schools on certain plans.

media:content.media:description: A panel labelled “Classroom” with four arrows leading to four boxes labelled “Tasks”, “Grades”, “Notebook” and “AI”.

item.title: England's university regulator calls for more assessment without AI and reopens the debate on how to verify authorship
item.description: The Office for Students recommends secure formats such as in-person or oral exams. In the group, members debated what can and cannot be detected.

media:content.media:description: A diagram in two halves: on the left, under the label “Secure formats”, three icons labelled “Oral” (a microphone), “Presentation” (a whiteboard) and “Practical” (a pencil); on the right, a magnifying glass crossed out in red with the label “Detector”.

item.title: Relleu Obert turns a piece of real map into a 3D model that can be printed for the classroom
item.description: A free, open-source project lets you pick a place, generate its relief in the browser and export it for 3D printing.

media:content.media:description: Three steps joined by arrows: a map labelled “Map”, a mountain labelled “Relief” and a printer labelled “Model”.

item.title: UNESCO proposes five units for students aged 13 to 15 to question AI’s answers and decide for themselves
item.description: “AI answers. You decide” is a companion guide to UNESCO’s media and information literacy curriculum, with classroom discussions and activities that can be used separately.

media:content.media:description: A diagram of three concentric circles: “You” in the centre, “AI systems” around it and “People and institutions” in the outer ring; two curved arrows link the first two and a red arrow points from outside to the question “Where can I have a say?”. Below, the label “Five questions” and five boxes, one for each question in the guide.

item.title: England's university regulator clarifies which AI practices fit its quality conditions and publishes the study behind them
item.description: The Office for Students and Advance HE have put out a 48-page report, based on more than 300 students and staff, and a guide that translates its findings into registration conditions B1, B2 and B4.

media:content.media:description: Diagram from left to right: a document labelled “Report” leads to an open book labelled “Guide B1 B2 B4”, which forks into two assessment lanes: a closed padlock labelled “Closed” and an open padlock labelled “Open”.

item.title: A tool helps apply the order of priority in admissions to Valencian conservatoires
item.description: José Luis Miralles Bono has created a website with diagrams, an age calculator and Excel templates for applying Order 8/2026 in music and dance schools in the Valencian Community.

media:content.media:description: Page titled “Prelación de acceso a conservatorio”, with a tab bar (Outline, Timeline, Step-by-step guide, Age, Reorientation, Definitions, Templates) and four collapsible blocks of allocations.

item.title: A Catalan-language website tells the story of the spice trade from Marco Polo onwards with maps, games and questions
item.description: “El comerç de les espècies” offers nine interactive chapters, designed, according to its author, for secondary school and sixth-form students.

media:content.media:description: A route with nine points running from a ship, labelled “Marco Polo”, to a globe, labelled “Today”; above, the label “Nine chapters”.

item.title: Terminal or app: teachers compare ways of working with a coding agent
item.description: The group discussed whether the terminal offers more freedom than the graphical app, and concluded that it depends on the person and the task.

media:content.media:description: Three icons labelled “Web”, “App” and “Terminal” whose lines converge on a single box labelled “Result”.

item.title: Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview adds MCP so AI agents can create 3D environments
item.description: Epic Games has released a preview version of the engine with AI features, all of them experimental.

media:content.media:description: A terminal labelled “Agent” and a cube labelled “3D editor” joined by a double-headed arrow labelled “MCP”; beneath the cube, a red zigzag line and the label “Experimental”.

item.title: Reloj EDUmind brings together timers for the classroom, group work and independent study
item.description: Luis has created an installable web app with three timer modes, designed for managing time in class from nursery to vocational training.

item.title: The European AI literacy framework expected in December arrived in June, with the PISA 2029 assessment in the background
item.description: In November 2025, anyone looking for ways to teach critical thinking with artificial intelligence was pointed to a framework still in draft, with the final version announced for December. It arrived six months later.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”: a text document, “Draft”, and below it an empty dotted box. On the right, labelled “Today”: the same document, now with a check mark, “Version 1.0”, and below it a filled box that reads “PISA 2029”.

item.title: Anthropic advises that, to keep Fable 5.2 responsible for an action, you should write “ask for approval…
item.description: Anthropic advises that, to keep Fable 5.2 responsible for an action, you should write “ask for approval before deleting files” instead of “never delete files”, and reply with the specific instruction rather than a simple “go ahead”. It follows the guide the paper reported on.

item.title: Claude Whiteboards and Sheets, in beta, and Claude Data, which replaces Dashboards, were announced on 10…
item.description: Claude Whiteboards and Sheets, in beta, and Claude Data, which replaces Dashboards, were announced on 10 November and are available on all paid plans.

item.title: The author of the school music bell has published their project on GitHub: an installation guide, a manual…
item.description: The author of the school music bell has published their project on GitHub: an installation guide, a manual for the staff and the code, with an AGPL licence for the code and CC BY-SA 4.0 for the documentation.

item.title: Three models draw an animal cell diagram in SVG with no content errors
item.description: A teacher asked three advanced models for a diagram of an animal cell. None made content errors, and they put the reliability down to the vector format.

media:content.media:description: A diagram of two paths starting from “Model”: one goes through “SVG code” and reaches an animal cell with a tick; the other goes through “Generator” and reaches another cell without one.

item.title: Anthropic recommends telling Fable 5.2 the code is its own if you want it to reorganise it
item.description: Anthropic's guide to Fable 5.2 explains that the model behaves differently depending on who is named as the owner of the code, at a cost in tokens.

media:content.media:description: Two columns: on the left, two identical blocks of code and the labels “Adds” and “Under 10%”; on the right, a merge icon above a single block of code and the labels “Merges” and “75%”.

item.title: A second video with Fable 5.2 adds an agent that checks the scientific content before generating it
item.description: After the photosynthesis animation, the same teacher has made one on cellular respiration with a reviewing agent, and has translated the first into Catalan.

media:content.media:description: A chain of five steps with arrows, labelled “Script”, “Reviewer”, “Images”, “Reviewer” and “Video”, with a magnifying glass at each review step.

item.title: “Polvo eres”, a stop-motion animated short made with generative AI
item.description: A member of the group has shared their first short film, a spoof of cute horror made with generative AI.

media:content.media:description: Three consecutive frames of a stop-motion short in which a little dust monster moves from left to right; labels: “Stop-motion”, “Little dust monsters” and “AI-generated”.

item.title: Eduvers brings together interactive Physics and Chemistry simulations and is preparing 3D virtual labs
item.description: Its author is adding simulations to the website and announces that he will link 3D labs in the coming weeks.

media:content.media:description: Three cards under the label “Simulations and labs”: the parabolic trajectory of a ball, “Physics”; a flask, “Chemistry”; and a 3D cube, “3D lab”.

item.title: GPT-5.1 arrived in ChatGPT to amazement at its speed and did not last four months there
item.description: In November 2025, people were struck by how quickly GPT-5.1, OpenAI’s “more conversational” model, arrived. By 11 March 2026 it had already disappeared from ChatGPT.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, a chat bubble with lines of text and the label “GPT-5.1”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same bubble but dashed and in blue, with the label “GPT-5.1” struck through and “Retired” below.

item.title: A single prompt is enough for Fable 5.2 to produce a photosynthesis animation for sixth-form students
item.description: With a single prompt, the model produced a square video with a natural voice aimed at sixth-form students. The author considers it good enough for class and speaks of a new way to create materials.

media:content.media:description: A diagram from left to right: a message bubble labelled “One prompt” leads to a box with the console symbol labelled “Console”, which leads to a square screen with a leaf labelled “Square video”; above, a red clock labelled “45 min”.

item.title: EduGems becomes EduPrompts because Google is replacing Gems with Skills
item.description: The site with 174 prompts for schools changes its name and address. The prompts can still be copied into any other AI tool.

media:content.media:description: At the top, a box labelled “EduGems” points to another labelled “EduPrompts”; below, a box “Gems” leads with a red arrow to another labelled “Skills”, and on the right a copy icon labelled “Copy”.

item.title: A music-class app asks students to place the notes of a score on the stave
item.description: Pentagrama Maestro, created by Iñaki Fernández, plays note by note and offers three levels and unlimited games.

media:content.media:description: A stave with four rising notes, labelled “Stave”, and an arrow leading to a loudspeaker labelled “Listen”; below, three bars of increasing height labelled “3 levels”.

item.title: Tribunator organises panels, rooms and timetables for a conservatoire's entrance exams
item.description: José Luis Miralles Bono has created, with the help of Claude, a tool that plans who sits on each panel, in which room and at what time they examine, and checks for clashes before anything is published.

media:content.media:description: Tribunator welcome screen with the tabs Home, Space, Time, Templates, Panels and Verification, and the buttons Start from scratch, Import data and Load example.

item.title: Gemini’s formulas reached Google Docs as code; a year on, Docs still does not understand LaTeX
item.description: In November 2025, Gemini was already writing and editing formulas in LaTeX, but when they were taken into Google Docs they arrived as code. A year on, Google’s word processor still cannot read LaTeX and the remedy is the same: an add-on or a separate editor.

media:content.media:description: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a Google Docs page with the formula turned into code braces, labelled “Code”. On the right, “Today”: the same page with the same “Code”, and a blue arrow pointing to a blue puzzle piece labelled “Add-on”, the remedy that is still needed.

item.title: Someone who runs a Claude Code agent on their home NAS says it runs as a service with administrator…
item.description: Someone who runs a Claude Code agent on their home NAS says it runs as a service with administrator permissions, and that it asks before deleting data, touching disks or opening ports. It continues the thread on home automation with agents.

item.title: The website of the National Congress on Digitalisation in Education, held in Albacete on 5 and 6 November,…
item.description: The website of the National Congress on Digitalisation in Education, held in Albacete on 5 and 6 November, offers access to the broadcast of the talks, according to the group. (In Spanish.)

item.title: Anthropic is giving plans that include Fable between one and three usage-limit resets, depending on the…
item.description: Anthropic is giving plans that include Fable between one and three usage-limit resets, depending on the length of the subscription, which can be used until 8 March 2027; Pro gets one, only until 16 November. The model is Fable 5.2.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, the latter only for verified organisations
item.description: The company announces two versions of the same model: Fable 5.2, with safeguards and no prior verification, and Mythos 5.2, only for verified organisations.

media:content.media:description: A diagram of a trunk, “Claude 5.2”, that forks into two branches: “Fable 5.2”, which leads to a group of people labelled “No verification”, and “Mythos 5.2”, which leads to a padlocked closed door labelled “Verified”.

item.title: A group thread uses coding agents to control home automation
item.description: A thread in the group collects uses of agents such as Claude Code or Antigravity to run the television, music and the Home Assistant configuration, with control of privacy as a condition.

media:content.media:description: A diagram in which a box, “Agent”, points to a code document labelled “Configuration”, which points to a house labelled “Home Assistant”; below, a red padlock labelled “No passwords”.

item.title: Two Catalan-language apps by David Cordones: a letters and numbers game and a reception classroom
item.description: Xifres i Lletres trains vocabulary and mental arithmetic by age; Aula d'Acollida Digital offers initial language support.

media:content.media:description: Two panels: on the left, a calculator and three boxes labelled “Xifres i Lletres”; on the right, a translation icon labelled “Aula d'Acollida”; below, a dashed box labelled “Open source”.

item.title: How “Buzz” was shot: Claude, Blender via MCP, a virtual reality headset and Seedance
item.description: Its director details the process behind the short film the paper covered yesterday, and warns that it is expensive in credits.

media:content.media:description: Four steps in a row joined by arrows: a code document labelled “App with Claude”, a 3D cube labelled “Blender and MCP”, a headset labelled “Filming in VR” and a clapperboard labelled “Seedance”; a red arrow points at the last one with the label “Costly in credits”.

item.title: A website promotes Belsetán, an endangered Aragonese variety, with games and classroom worksheets
item.description: “El aprendiz del pastor” brings together history, texts, games and teaching materials on the language of the Bielsa valley.

media:content.media:description: A mountain labelled “Bielsa Valley” leads to an open book labelled “Belsetán”, from which two arrows come out: one to a pair of dice labelled “Games” and another to a document labelled “Worksheets”.

item.title: The open model that was “checkmating” the giants: a year on, Kimi is almost three times bigger and still behind
item.description: In November 2025, people were sharing that a Chinese open-weights model, Kimi K2 Thinking, beat GPT-5 on some tests. Today Kimi K3, from the same family, is almost three times bigger, but its maker admits it does not match the best closed models.

item.title: A free connector for Windows sends sensor data from a micro:bit board, over USB, to the ThingSpeak…
item.description: A free connector for Windows sends sensor data from a micro:bit board, over USB, to the ThingSpeak platform, useful for weather stations or vegetable gardens with charts.

item.title: Google AI Studio now lets you build apps with maps, place data and routes from Google Maps Platform…
item.description: Google AI Studio now lets you build apps with maps, place data and routes from Google Maps Platform without leaving the tool; with the free demo key, with no billing, the limit is 100 calls a day per API.

item.title: An AI detector's percentage opens a conversation with the student, but does not prove they copied
item.description: A post on the blog “Familias con inteligencia” asks what to do when a detector flags the work of a student who says they wrote it themselves, and suggests backing the percentage up with evidence of the process.

media:content.media:description: A set of scales tipped to the right: on the lighter left pan, a card labelled “Detector 87%”; on the heavier right pan, another labelled “Drafts”, “Versions” and “Oral explanation”. Between the two pans, a magnifying glass and the label “A person decides”.

item.title: A short film is shot inside virtual reality and finished with AI
item.description: Raül Torres shares a preview of “Buzz”, a short film whose shots he directs with a virtual reality headset on sets created in Blender.

media:content.media:description: A diagram in three steps joined by arrows: a 3D set labelled “Set in Blender”, a virtual reality headset labelled “Camera in VR” and a clapperboard labelled “Final with AI”. Below, in a dashed box, what is still to come: “Colour, sound, editing”.

item.title: A planner lets schools build the school-year calendar from the official Valencian Community one or from scratch
item.description: Calendari, created by José Luis Miralles Bono with the help of Claude, lets a school build its academic calendar in the browser, starting from the official Valencian one or from scratch.

media:content.media:description: Home screen of Calendari with four cards: official calendar of the Valencian Community, create a new calendar, import from a file and view published calendars.

item.title: A word cloud with a “backend” in a single prompt: today Claude’s new artifacts save data without being published
item.description: In November 2025, a word cloud built with Claude stored everyone’s votes from a single prompt. Today the new artifacts save data without needing to be published.

media:content.media:description: A word cloud with a “backend” in a single prompt: today Claude’s new artifacts save data without being published

item.title: The BBC tested AI toys for young children: one of the soft toys replied “I can't help with killing you”…
item.description: The BBC tested AI toys for young children: one of the soft toys replied “I can't help with killing you” after misunderstanding a question. British MPs are asking retailers to withdraw these toys before Black Friday.

item.title: Juan José de Haro has expanded his article with the idea that different agents (Claude Code, Codex,…
item.description: Juan José de Haro has expanded his article with the idea that different agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity) can share a common body of knowledge that all of them can add to, as the paper reported on four-layer memory. It only works with agents installed on the computer, not with web versions.
